key_insight: A general-relativistic superfluid framework establishes necessary and sufficient conditions for nonlinear causality and strong hyperbolicity, enabling stable simulations of neutron-star vortex dynamics.
engineering_relevance: The framework provides a computational foundation for studying superfluid transport, rotational dynamics, and pulsar-glitch mechanisms in neutron-star interiors.
method: Model entrainment, vortex forces, and vortex line energy in relativistic two-fluid hydrodynamics.
Recast vortex dynamics using effective electric and magnetic fields inspired by force-free electrodynamics.
Combine finite-volume evolution with constrained transport of vorticity and implicit electric-field updates.
evidence_signal: Validation includes an exact relativistic superfluid Riemann solution, Kelvin-wave dispersion relations, and neutron-star oscillation modes; a simplified spin-down simulation retains vortex twist and residual differential rotation.
watch_item: Vortex release and repinning are prescribed in the spin-down example, limiting conclusions about self-consistent glitch dynamics.
paper_title: Nonlinearly Causal General-Relativistic Superfluid Hydrodynamics: Simulating Vortex Dynamics in Neutron-Star Interiors
